endorsements.quote: A pilot clearing the 70-point aggregate threshold receives a “Conditional Scale” decision only if no individual domain score falls below afloor of 5 out of 10.
This finding supports a staged scale-up approach rather than immediate enterprise-wide deployment following early pilot success.

unlisted_practices: Governance councils should use weighted, lifecycle-stage scorecards with explicit domain weights to evaluate AI tools at defined gates (Vendor Evaluation, Pilot, Scale, Maintenance).

Governance scorecards should include business and operational execution domains (ROI/total cost of ownership, operational integration, vendor partnership execution) alongside safety, ethics, and equity.
Governance councils should test the sensitivity of scorecard weights and scores using one-way, stakeholder-scenario, and Monte Carlo analyses.
Governance councils should treat reviewer disagreement above a predefined threshold as a trigger for a mandatory governing-question discussion rather than forced re-scoring.
When unresolved high-stakes reviewer disagreement persists, governance councils should default the decision to extended pilot or small-scale pilot rather than scale progression.
Governance councils should require a minimum domain score floor in addition to an aggregate score threshold before approving progression from pilot to scale.
Governance frameworks should be designed as organizational learning mechanisms that support iterative improvement and treat unsuccessful pilots as sources of learning rather than terminal failures.

screen.reason: This paper presents a clinical AI governance framework (C-TACT) and scorecards with an illustrative retrospective demonstration, serving primarily as a framework/recommendation piece for healthcare organizations.
